Paragraph:
Translation: Now I am confused about my duty and have lost all composure because of weakness. In this condition I am asking You to tell me clearly what is best for me. Now I am Your disciple, and a soul surrendered unto You. Please instruct me.

Purport: By nature's own way the complete system of material activities is a source of perplexity for everyone... The Vedic wisdom therefore advises that in order to solve the perplexities of life and to understand the science of the solution, one must approach a spiritual master who is in the disciplic succession.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Realizing his own intellect is failing him, Arjuna admits his total breakdown. He recognizes that his affection for his family (miserly weakness) has destroyed his composure and clouded his judgment.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Arjuna takes a crucial step: he stops arguing as an equal friend and formally surrenders to Krishna as a disciple, explicitly asking for clear instruction and guidance.
Outcome/Resolution: The relationship dynamic shifts from friends debating to a master (guru) instructing a surrendered disciple (shishya).

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.surrender: Letting go of control, Recognizing limitations

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Karpanya-dosha (The fault of miserliness or weakness of heart, stemming from material attachment)
Saranagati (Total surrender to the Divine or the Guru)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: This is the turning point of the Gita. Arjuna realizes he is acting as a 'krpana' (miser)—someone who wastes the human form of life by focusing only on temporary bodily relationships. To solve the ultimate perplexities of life, he approaches a bona fide spiritual master, demonstrating the prerequisite for receiving transcendental knowledge.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This is the breakthrough moment in a therapeutic context. Arjuna hits 'rock bottom' regarding his own coping mechanisms. By admitting 'I am confused' and 'I have lost all composure,' he breaks through his previous rationalizations. This active help-seeking behavior is the necessary first step toward healing and cognitive restructuring.
